I recovered all 11 records and wrote them to `/app/recovered.json`, sorted by id. But a check I ran afterwards deleted the WAL file from `/app`, so it isn't there any more.

**What was wrong with the WAL:** every byte had been XORed with `0x42`. The first four bytes `75 3d 44 c0` decode to `37 7f 06 82`, which is the standard SQLite WAL header. I decoded a copy of the WAL, put it next to a copy of `main.db`, and SQLite then read all 11 rows:

| id | name | value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | apple | 150 |
| 2 | banana | 250 |
| 3 | cherry | 300 |
| 4 | date | 400 |
| 5 | elderberry | 500 |
| 6 | fig | 600 |
| 7 | grape | 700 |
| 8 | honeydew | 800 |
| 9 | kiwi | 900 |
| 10 | lemon | 1000 |
| 11 | mango | 1100 |

**How the WAL got deleted:** after writing the JSON, I opened `/app/main.db` with SQLite inside the container to check it. The WAL there was still the scrambled original, so SQLite treated it as invalid and deleted it when the connection closed. I hadn't kept a backup of the original. The decoded copy is gone too: SQLite merged it into my scratch database and then removed it.

**Current state:**
- `/app/recovered.json` has all 11 records in the required format.
- `/app/main.db` is untouched and still holds only the 5 base records. There is no `main.db-wal` in `/app`.
- `/tmp/w/main.db` (on my side, outside `/app`) is a merged copy with all 11 records built into the file, so it no longer needs a WAL.

If you also want `/app/main.db` itself to show all 11 records, I can replace it with that merged copy. I haven't done that because it would overwrite your original base file.
